title: Claim Delayed by False Policy Records
text:
I had an active Lemonade Pet Insurance policy for my dog,  since September 2024 and never had an issue until this year.

My monthly premium unexpectedly jumped from $89 to $114, and when I filed a very simple claim, everything unraveled.

First, I was told Lemonade “did not have my dog’s medical history,” despite the fact that nothing had changed and coverage had been active for over a year and we had previous claims. After I provided documentation again, I was then told that Storm allegedly had a previous insurance policy with a company called “GAP.”

I have never had pet insurance with any other provider in the United States, and I moved to America in 2024. I don’t even know what GAP is. There is no prior or secondary policy, yet Lemonade repeatedly insisted on this and requested proof of cancellation for a policy that never existed.

This has caused unnecessary delays, confusion, and stress over what should have been a straightforward claim. The experience revealed serious internal record-keeping or file-matching issues, and customer service continued to push the same incorrect information instead of resolving the error.

Between the sudden premium increase and the repeated administrative mishaps, I’ve lost confidence in this provider and will be cancelling my policy and finding coverage elsewhere.

title: Software errors like this are unacceptable in 2025
text: Lemonade is recommended for renters insurance by Forbes, so you'd think that would be a good thing. Unfortunately the Lemonade.com website has some significant software errors. When you're satisfied with your quote the checkout system offers you payment by credit care or by checking account. Gone are the days when you could manually enter your bank routing number and checking account number. Lemonade uses the Plaid service, prompting you to share your online banking login and password. If you do so, Plaid will reset and bring  you back to the start to provide your login and password again. And again, And again. Then Lemonade logs you out of their site. If you choose to pay by card, many card types will be rejected (for example Visa debit gift cards) but Lemonade won't tell you why it rejected the card nor what cards are acceptable. I spent a lot of time trying to give Lemonade my business but they kept failing a simple online purchase transaction that I could accomplish in 1995. I phoned Lemonade and gamed the phone system menu to reach an actual human. He told me that the only way Lemonade sells insurance policies is through the website, no human assistance is available. Then he recommended I clear my browser's cache and disabled pop-up blockers, which I have been doing since 1995. So, Lemonade has excellent prices for a range of insurance policies, but you'll need a lot of luck to complete the purchase. NOT RECOMMENDED.

title: Report to state legislatures for consumer fraud.
text:
I filed a claim for significant water damage that destroyed my property and resulted in microbial growth. Instead of contacting me, the paying policyholder, my assigned adjuster, Sasha, chose to contact my landlord first. She claimed this was “protocol,” yet proceeded to send my landlord a series of irrelevant, intrusive, and entirely inappropriate questions—including inquiries about what type of tenant I am and whether I pay my bills on time. These questions had absolutely nothing to do with the cause or extent of the water damage.
It is clear she wanted to gather biased information before ever speaking to me, the customer whose premiums fund this company.
When I reached out after discovering this, she was openly hostile, rude, dismissive, and behaved as though handling my claim was some sort of charity instead of a service I am paying for. She denied my claim without conducting any legitimate investigation, refused to let me explain the damages, and incorrectly stated that microbial growth is not covered—despite the fact that the water damage itself, which caused the microbial growth, is covered under the policy.
I requested escalation to her manager, Chad, who was equally unhelpful. He made no effort to meaningfully engage, sent a random email with no scheduled follow-up, and provided no resolution whatsoever.
At this point, it appears Lemonade is more committed to denying valid claims than honoring the coverage their customers pay for. The treatment I received was dismissive, disrespectful, and entirely unacceptable. If this is how claims are handled, it raises serious concerns about their business practices and compliance.
I am now forced to escalate further, including exploring legal action. I strongly encourage consumers to contact their state insurance regulator and legislators to report these practices. Insurance companies cannot continue taking customers’ money while arbitrarily denying coverage and mistreating the very people they claim to protect.

text:

What was a good price came at a cost.

title: Very Disappointing Experience — Avoid
text:
I purchased Lemonade Pet Insurance for peace of mind and support in case my cat ever needed urgent care. Unfortunately, when my cat, Mercy, recently developed an upper respiratory infection (URI), my claim was denied.

Lemonade classified the condition as pre-existing because Mercy had similar symptoms about 10 months ago. Even though upper respiratory infections in cats are typically acute, not chronic, and can occur multiple times in their lifetime (similar to the flu in humans), Lemonade decided that any recurrence within 12 months is not covered.

They denied coverage for this common, treatable condition by labeling it “pre-existing.” Their reasoning? Mercy had a URI more than ten months before the policy start date, and they require a full 12 months without any symptoms to consider a condition “cured.”

This interpretation makes routine illnesses practically uninsurable. By their logic, if a cat gets a cold once, they can refuse coverage for any similar illness unless 12 months pass with zero related symptoms. That is simply not realistic for pets — and they know it.

When I requested clarification, I received generic policy language instead of genuine review or support. The policy clearly prioritizes the company’s benefit over the animal’s wellbeing and the paying customer.

I will not be renewing and do not recommend Lemonade Pet Insurance. Be cautious — their definition of “pre-existing condition” is extremely broad and can easily be used to deny legitimate claims for common, unrelated illnesses. Pets deserve better, and so do responsible pet owners.

a move-out statement,

a new lease, or

I gathered and sent all of the requested documents the very next day (October 14, 2025). I even followed up several times to make sure they received everything. Despite going above and beyond, Lemonade later claimed I had not provided the proper information — even though I sent exactly what their email listed.

It’s not about the small refund amount ($21.33 per month) — it’s about how poorly this company handles cancellations and how broken their app experience is. It’s easy to buy a policy, but nearly impossible to cancel one. No confirmation, no clear process, and lots of back-and-forth emails that lead nowhere.

Lemonade promotes itself as simple, fast, and transparent, but my experience was the opposite. Until they fix the app design and start treating customers fairly when they cancel, I cannot recommend Lemonade Insurance.
